results.message: What did Augustine mean by "love, and do what you will"?

voice_event.speaker: lpc
voice_event.text: Augustine opened the story of his own life with a restless heart. He named that condition in one sentence: "Thou hast formed us for Thyself, and our hearts are restless till they find rest in Thee." He also wrote on forgiving someone who is not sorry. Loving an enemy who still wishes you ill is a higher thing than only doing good to one who has never harmed you. He named it as obeying Christ's own command to love enemies and pray for those who persecute you. He called this the highest standard, one only the most perfect reach in full, though he held every believer should strive for it, sorry or not. He held a second, more ordinary standard too. When someone who has sinned against you asks forgiveness, and you forgive him from the heart, that much fulfills what the Lord's Prayer itself asks of us.

names.name: Augustinius of Hippo Regius, presbyter 391, bishop 395/396-430

figures_used.bridge_line: Our bishop at Hippo. The people seized him and brought him to be made a presbyter while he wept. Later they pressed him into the bishop's office over his own refusal. He spent his last days weeping over psalms of penitence, while an army lay outside the walls.

dates.display: converted 386, baptised 387; seized by the congregation at Hippo and ordained presbyter against his own wishes in 391, weeping through it (Possidius, Vita IV); designated coadjutor and consecrated bishop of Hippo by Megalius, primate of Numidia, in 395/396, again amid popular acclamation (Possidius, Vita VIII); died 430, during the Vandal siege of Hippo
